From 9b68a1cc966bc947d00e4c0df7722d118125aa37 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ding Hui <dinghui@sangfor.com.cn>
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 15:21:10 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/bnxt_re: Fix OOB write in bnxt_re_copy_err_stats()

Commit ef56081d1864 ("RDMA/bnxt_re: RoCE related hardware counters
update") added three new counters and placed them after
BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR.

BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR acts as a boundary marker for allocating hardware
statistics with different num_counters values on chip_gen_p5_p7 devices.

As a result, BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS are used when allocating
hw_stats, which leads to an out-of-bounds write in
bnxt_re_copy_err_stats().

The counters BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, and
BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS are applicable to generic hardware, not
only p5/p7 devices.

Fix this by moving these counters before BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR so they
are included in the generic counter set.

Fixes: ef56081d1864 ("RDMA/bnxt_re: RoCE related hardware counters update")
Reported-by: Yingying Zheng <zhengyingying@sangfor.com.cn>
Signed-off-by: Ding Hui <dinghui@sangfor.com.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251208072110.28874-1-dinghui@sangfor.com.cn
Reviewed-by: Kalesh AP <kalesh-anakkur.purayil@broadcom.com>
Tested-by: Kalesh AP <kalesh-anakkur.purayil@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/hw_counters.h b/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/hw_counters.h
index 09d371d442aa..cebec033f4a0 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/hw_counters.h
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/hw_counters.h
@@ -89,6 +89,9 @@ enum bnxt_re_hw_stats {
 	BNXT_RE_RES_SRQ_LOAD_ERR,
 	BNXT_RE_RES_TX_PCI_ERR,
 	BNXT_RE_RES_RX_PCI_ERR,
+	BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR,
+	BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR,
+	BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS,
 	BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR,
 	BNXT_RE_TX_ATOMIC_REQ,
 	BNXT_RE_TX_READ_REQ,
@@ -110,9 +113,6 @@ enum bnxt_re_hw_stats {
 	BNXT_RE_TX_CNP,
 	BNXT_RE_RX_CNP,
 	BNXT_RE_RX_ECN,
-	BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR,
-	BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR,
-	BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS,
 	BNXT_RE_NUM_EXT_COUNTERS
 };
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies the `bnxt_re_hw_stats` enum in `drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/hw_counters.h` to fix an out-of-bounds (OOB) write issue. Specifically, it moves three counter definitions (`BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR`, `BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR`, `BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS`) from after `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR` to before it. This repositioning ensures these counters are included in the standard counter set (up to `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR`) rather than the extended set, preventing an OOB write in `bnxt_re_copy_err_stats()` when hardware statistics are allocated for `chip_gen_p5_p7` devices. The fix corrects a boundary error introduced by a previous commit.

RDMA/bnxt_re: Fix OOB write in bnxt_re_copy_err_stats()

Commit ef56081d1864 ("RDMA/bnxt_re: RoCE related hardware counters
update") added three new counters and placed them after
BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR.

BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR acts as a boundary marker for allocating hardware
statistics with different num_counters values on chip_gen_p5_p7 devices.

As a result, BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS are used when allocating
hw_stats, which leads to an out-of-bounds write in
bnxt_re_copy_err_stats().

The counters BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, and
BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS are applicable to generic hardware, not
only p5/p7 devices.

Fix this by moving these counters before BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR so they
are included in the generic counter set.

Fixes: ef56081d1864 ("RDMA/bnxt_re: RoCE related hardware counters update")
Reported-by: Yingying Zheng <zhengyingying@sangfor.com.cn>
Signed-off-by: Ding Hui <dinghui@sangfor.com.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251208072110.28874-1-dinghui@sangfor.com.cn
Reviewed-by: Kalesh AP <kalesh-anakkur.purayil@broadcom.com>
Tested-by: Kalesh AP <kalesh-anakkur.purayil@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The enum `bnxt_re_hw_stats` had three counters (`BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR`, `BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR`, `BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS`) placed after `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR`. Since `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR` is used as a boundary for allocating hardware statistics (standard counters vs. extended counters) on `chip_gen_p5_p7` devices, these three counters were not included in the standard counter set (`BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS`). However, `bnxt_re_copy_err_stats()` likely references these counters assuming they exist within the allocated block, leading to an out-of-bounds write when copying statistics from hardware to the allocated buffer.

Here is the patch:
 	BNXT_RE_RES_TX_PCI_ERR,
 	BNXT_RE_RES_RX_PCI_ERR,
+	BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR,
+	BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR,
+	BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS,
 	BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR,
 	BNXT_RE_TX_ATOMIC_REQ,
 	BNXT_RE_RX_CNP,
 	BNXT_RE_RX_ECN,
-	BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR,
-	BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR,
-	BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS,
 	BNXT_RE_NUM_EXT_COUNTERS
 };

<text>// Enum with three counters placed after BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR
    BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR,
    BNXT_RE_TX_ATOMIC_REQ,
    BNXT_RE_RX_CNP,
    BNXT_RE_RX_ECN,
    BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR,
    BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR,
    BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS,
    BNXT_RE_NUM_EXT_COUNTERS
};</text>
<text>// Allocation of hw_stats using standard counters count (which excludes those three)
    hw_stats = kcalloc(BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS, sizeof(*hw_stats), GFP_KERNEL);</text>
<text>// In bnxt_re_copy_err_stats(), accessing indices like BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR writes beyond buffer.</text>
Reason:
The three new counters were added after BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR, which defines the boundary for standard counters. Since BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS counts up to that boundary, the allocated buffer is too small to include these counters. When bnxt_re_copy_err_stats() writes to those indices, an out‑of‑bounds write occurs.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>// Move the three counters before BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR in the enum
    BNXT_RE_RES_RX_PCI_ERR,
    BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR,
    BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR,
    BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS,
    BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR,
    BNXT_RE_TX_ATOMIC_REQ,
    // ... (remaining counters unchanged)</text>
<text>// (Allocation and copy functions remain the same; buffer now includes all needed indices)</text>
Reason:
By placing the three counters before BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR, they become part of the standard counter set. BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS now includes them, so the allocated buffer has sufficient space. bnxt_re_copy_err_stats() can safely write to these indices without overrunning the buffer.
